newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse eases, reverses record run.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse eases, reverses record run.

text.p: The Hungarian share market reversed from a seven-session bull run on Friday and closed a shade lower with declining buying interest, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 7,874.83 points, down 5.33.

"Foreigners are less active, domestic investors have scaled down their activities due to holidays," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings. "The market turned uncertain as the index was at a very high level."

The Budapest Stock Exchange's BUX index has risen just over 90 percent this year in forint terms, benefiting from an economic recovery, strong corporate earnings growth, a strong dollar, and fresh capital seeking investment opportunities.

Andrea Dicso, analyst at Bank Austria-Investment said she expected relatively quiet days to come next week, but added the market might continue to rise after that as more high caps release their first half earnings.
"I expect the market to take a wait-and-see stance next week, possibly with slight profit-taking," she said.
"But the week after next week prices might recover on further good corporate earnings, from (oil firm) MOL and OTP OTP.BU."
Hungarian companies have to release their first half figures by August 15.
Newcomer North American Bus Industries NABI took a flying start on its first day, trading well above its 3,280 forint IPO price. It closed at 4,800 forints.

Companies that released their first half earnings closed mixed, with Inter-Europa Bank finishing at 52,000 forints, down 3,050; plastics maker Pannonplast at 11,700 forints, down 250 and Human at 4,100, up 50.
